The Problem: Why Traditional Methods Fall Short
Traditional (Agile/Scrum)
• Sprints: 2–6 weeks
• Daily standups, retros
• Siloed roles (FE, BE, DevOps)
• Manual planning & estimation
• Design techniques optional
• Story points & velocity
AI-Era Reality
• Iteration in hours/days
• Continuous feedback loops
• AI collapses specializations
• AI handles decomposition
• Design must be baked in
• Business Value over velocity
Key Insight: Retrofitting AI into Agile limits its potential and reinforces outdated inefficiencies. We need automobiles, not faster horse chariots.
© 2026, Amazon Web Services, Inc. or its affiliates.
3
Two Paradigms: AI-Assisted vs. AI-Driven
AI-Assisted (Current Era)
• Human drives the workflow
• AI augments specific tasks
• Code autocomplete, bug detection
• Developer initiates every action

Limitation: Doesn't unlock AI's full potential
AI-Driven (AI-DLC)
• AI drives the workflow
• Human validates & approves
• AI plans, decomposes, generates
• AI initiates conversations

Advantage: Full AI leverage + human oversight
Analogy: Google Maps — you set the destination (intent), the system plans the route and gives directions. You maintain oversight and can override at any time.

SECTION 01
10 Key Principles
© 2026, Amazon Web Services, Inc. or its affiliates.
5
Key Principles (1–5)
1. Reimagine Rather Than Retrofit — Build from first principles, not faster horse chariots
2. Reverse the Conversation Direction — AI initiates & directs; humans approve
3. Integrate Design Techniques — DDD/BDD/TDD baked in, not optional
4. Align With AI Capability — Realistic about current AI; devs retain oversight
5. Cater to Complex Systems — Multiple teams, trade-offs, scalability needs
© 2026, Amazon Web Services, Inc. or its affiliates.
6
Key Principles (6–10)
6. Retain What Enhances Human Symbiosis — User stories, risk registers stay
7. Facilitate Transition Through Familiarity — Orient in a day; Sprints → Bolts
8. Streamline Responsibilities — AI collapses specialization silos
9. Minimise Stages, Maximise Flow — Fewer handoffs; checkpoints as "loss functions"
10. No Hard-Wired Workflows — AI recommends plans; humans validate iteratively

Three Phases of AI-DLC
1. Inception
Goal: Elaborate intent → plan

Ritual: Mob Elaboration

AI: Generates plan, proposes bounded contexts

Human: Validates, adjusts, approves
2. Construction
Goal: Build in Bolts

Ritual: Mob Programming

AI: Decomposes → designs → codes → tests

Human: Reviews at each gate
3. Operations
Goal: Deploy & maintain

Ritual: Continuous monitoring

AI: IaC, monitoring, optimization

Human: Approves deploys, incidents

The Workflow: How AI Drives Development
Developer sets INTENT (the destination)
↓
AI generates Level 1 Plan (decomposition, contexts, stories)
↓
Human VALIDATES / ADJUSTS the plan
↓
AI recursively decomposes → Domain → Logical → Code
↓
Human validates at each gate ("loss function" checkpoints)
↓
Deployment & Operations

11
Green-Field Example: Recommendation Engine
Intent: "Build a recommendation engine for cross-selling products"
INCEPTION
AI decomposes into bounded contexts: User Profile, Product Catalog, Recommendation Logic, Analytics
Mob Elaboration produces domain models + user stories for each context
CONSTRUCTION
Each bounded context built in parallel Bolts
AI generates code → developer validates → continuous integration
OPERATIONS
AI generates IaC, monitoring dashboards, optimization loops
© 2026, Amazon Web Services, Inc. or its affiliates.
12
Brown-Field: Working With Existing Systems
Same AI-DLC flow, but with an additional step before Construction:
Step 1: AI reverse-engineers existing code into domain models (static + dynamic)
Step 2: Human validates AI's understanding of the current system
Step 3: Proceed with normal Construction phase (Bolts, code generation, validation)
This enables AI-DLC to work with legacy codebases — not just greenfield projects.

Critical Thinking: Strengths & Limitations
Strengths
• Embraces AI's actual capabilities
• DDD ensures quality isn't sacrificed
• Realistic about human oversight
• Designed for enterprise systems
Limitations
• Requires mature AI tooling
• Assumes developer comfort with AI
• "Hours/days" claim is optimistic
• Not relevant for simple CRUD apps
Questions to Consider:
1. What if AI makes a wrong architectural decision early?
2. How to maintain institutional knowledge when AI drives decisions?
3. Is "reversed conversation" comfortable for all developers?
4. How do regulated industries adapt the approval gates?

15
SUMMARY
Key Takeaways
1. AI-DLC reimagines (not retrofits) development for the AI era
2. AI drives, humans validate — conversation direction is reversed
3. Design techniques are built in, not optional add-ons
4. Bolts replace Sprints — iteration in hours/days
5. Three phases: Inception → Construction → Operations
6. Target: complex systems with trade-offs & multiple teams
7. Familiarity enables adoption — practitioners can start in a day
